authorship.role: Independent read-only final artifact identity, saved geometry and saved-display-state reviewer; no production, test or documentation source edits. Not third-party or physical certification.

blender_supplement.scope: Sampled derivative transformation/visibility verification only, not collision, physics or continuous interpolation. The Blender verifier reports source_cad_hash_checked=false; this separate artifact review checks the current native CAD SHA against its recorded CAD identity. Full matrices and blend bytes are identified by hash, not embedded.

expansion.scope: Six spare holes for future small attachments or purchased spacers. This is a project expansion row, not an industry PCB pattern. Installed hardware and occupied device bodies may prevent simultaneous use of neighboring holes. No adapter, arbitrary extension load or spacer height is qualified merely by these bores.

common_plate_contract.scope: One centred rounded rectangular plate and twenty-hole template, without projecting utility tabs. The three rail carriers are identical physical prints including the rail shoe and structural tower datum. The optional power deck uses the same plate template on its integral tower. The outline is symmetric; the complete part retains oriented device holes and a rail clamp, so do not infer half-turn mounting equivalence. FC/P-AS patterns and spare board patterns are alternative uses, not permission to populate overlapping equipment simultaneously. Optical sensor tray remains an uninterrupted adhesive surface.

patterns.evidence: Manufacturer lists 20 x 20 mm and M2/M3 screw or grommet compatibility; this carrier supports the M2 option only.
Manufacturer lists a 30.5 mm mounting pattern and supplied M3 vibration standoffs.

standard_mounting.scope: Common board pitches for future alternative installations, not a universal board or connector fit. Use M2 on the 20 mm pattern and M3 on the 30.5 mm pattern. Printed holes are clearance bores, without threads or installed hardware. Choose purchased spacers and screw lengths after checking the actual device, insulation, underside access and wiring. These board patterns do not replace the separate structural tower attachment or qualify another device in an occupied bay.

For the underside radio, detach the carrier from the rail and remove the device along carrier-Z on the bench. When this carrier hosts the optical stack, detach the carrier for bench access, support the tower, remove both foot nuts and withdraw both foot screws downward before lifting the complete tower along optical+Z. The balloon is not modeled, so in-place underside access is not established. Bare-device path, not a connected harness.

common_carrier_identity.scope: Scalar, saved metadata and observed BREP byte identity supplement required source-bound native geometry equivalence; serialization order is not treated as a geometric criterion. Physical fasteners, adhesive, arbitrary extensions and all holes used simultaneously remain unqualified.

independent_preview_document_review.scope: Independent visual reading of eight final previews and consistency review of seven current layout documents. No image-derived dimensions, collision proof, physical retention, load qualification, new manufacturer-source verification or complete native validation claim.

limits: Passing checks establish source/artifact identity and the declared nominal CAD envelope checks, not production or flight release.

Eight nominal functional interfaces in the mechanism remain separately classified; physical manufacturing fits, motion under load, wire behavior and actual interfaces remain qualified only by future bench checks.
